request.text: What is the current on AM1?

solution.item: Solution by TINA assisted by AI
First we calculate the total resistance between the generator nodes (VS1)
R2 and AM1 connected in series so Rb=R2+RAM1=1kOhm+0Ohm=1kOhm
Rb and R1 connected in series so Ra=Rb+R1=1kOhm+1kOhm=2kOhm
The total resistance is Ra = 2kOhm
Now we calculate the current on AM1
We know that the voltage between VS1 nodes is 5 Volt.
The components Rb and R1 connected in series.
The voltage between this components starting and ending node is 5 Volt
Rb is in the voltage divider so the voltage on Rb is Rb/Ra*5 Volt = 2.5 Volt
The current in branch Ra is 'voltage on this branch'/'impedance in this branch' = 5/2k = 2.5m Amper
The current on Rb is the current on Ra. Therefore the current on Rb is 2.5m Amper
The components Rb and R1 connected in series.
The voltage between this components starting and ending node is 5 Volt
R1 is in the voltage divider so the voltage on R1 is R1/Ra*5 Volt = 2.5 Volt
The current in branch Ra is 'voltage on this branch'/'impedance in this branch' = 5/2k = 2.5m Amper
The current on R1 is the current on Ra. Therefore the current on R1 is 2.5m Amper
The components R2 and AM1 connected in series.
The voltage between this components starting and ending node is 2.5 Volt
R2 is in the voltage divider so the voltage on R2 is R2/Rb*2.5 Volt = 2.5 Volt
The current in branch Rb is 'voltage on this branch'/'impedance in this branch' = 2.5/1k = 2.5m Amper
The current on R2 is the current on Rb. Therefore the current on R2 is 2.5m Amper
The components R2 and AM1 connected in series.
The voltage between this components starting and ending node is 2.5 Volt
The current in branch Rb is 'voltage on this branch'/'impedance in this branch' = 2.5/1k = 2.5m Amper
The current on AM1 is the current on Rb. Therefore the current on AM1 is -2.5m Amper
